channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Astana Traffic Accidents Increase by Over 17 Percent Despite Crime Reduction
item.description: In Astana, traffic accidents rose by 17.5% in the first nine months of the year, according to police. While overall crime decreased by 17.5% and internet fraud by 15.1%, authorities acknowledge problematic issues in road safety. Measures including drone usage are being intensified to improve traffic safety.

item.title: Uzbek President arrives in Turkmenistan for working visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrived in Turkmenistan on October 7 for a working visit. He will attend the 8th Consultative Meeting of Central Asian and Azerbaijani Heads of State on October 8 and the CIS Summit on October 9. Bilateral meetings are also planned on the sidelines of these events.

item.title: Reconstruction of Dostlik canal connecting Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan begins
item.description: Reconstruction of a 3.4 km section of the Dostlik canal, passing through Gulistan city, has begun. The 77.2 billion soum project includes concreting the canal to reduce water loss. A 5.62 km road and a 1.02 km pedestrian path will be built alongside, with surrounding areas to be improved.

item.title: Uzbek President reviews proposals for new Ministry of Education and Science
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals for organizing the activities of the new Ministry of Education and Science. The ministry was formed by merging previous education bodies to create a unified system, improve quality, and enhance human capital development. Key tasks include ensuring continuity and aligning education with labor market needs.

item.title: CIS Countries Advocate for Complete Ban on Placing Weapons in Outer Space
item.description: CIS foreign ministers, meeting in Avaza, Turkmenistan, adopted a statement supporting practical steps to prevent an arms race in outer space. They approved a plan for inter-ministerial consultations for 2027 and endorsed measures to deepen integration in cultural, humanitarian, and security spheres.

item.title: Nukus Pedagogical Institute Implements Dual Education System for Preschool Teachers
item.description: The Nukus State Pedagogical Institute named after Ajiniyaz has introduced a dual education system for preschool education majors starting from the 2026-2027 academic year. Over 400 educators with secondary specialized education are enrolled. This system combines theoretical knowledge with practical experience, aiming to better prepare future specialists for the labor market's demands.

item.title: Fergana Programmer's AI Project Wins International ASOCIO Digital & AI Awards
item.description: Muhammadqodir Abduvoitov, a programmer from Fergana, has won an international award at the ASOCIO Digital & AI Awards 2026 in Indonesia for his startup, Braille Recognition. The project, recognized in the 'AI for Public Good' category, is a mobile app that uses a smartphone camera to read Braille and convert it into text, aiding visually impaired individuals.

item.title: Investigation Launched into Deaths of Two Teenagers in Oral, Kazakhstan
item.description: An investigation has been launched into the deaths of two teenagers, born in 2010 and 2012, in Oral, Kazakhstan. The West Kazakhstan region police department confirmed that pre-trial proceedings are underway to determine the causes and circumstances of the incident. Information is being withheld in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Code.

item.title: Russia signals tougher stance on Armenia's EU aspirations
item.description: Russia is adopting a harder line towards Armenia's efforts to join the European Union. Moscow may use force to keep Yerevan aligned, potentially suspending nuclear cooperation with the US and requiring Rosatom to build Armenia's next reactor. Armenia has increasingly defied Russia, downgrading security ties and reorienting its economy towards the EU.

item.title: UAE joins Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in trans-Afghan railway project
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have signed a memorandum of understanding with the United Arab Emirates for the development of a trans-Afghan railway. This project aims to provide Central Asian exports access to Pakistani seaports. The UAE's involvement addresses the financial and technical shortcomings of the Central Asian states in realizing this infrastructure goal.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Russian Delegation to Discuss Trade and Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with a Russian delegation led by First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov. They discussed practical implementation of agreements from high-level meetings, noting steady growth in mutual trade and cooperation in industry, energy, and other sectors. Both sides emphasized increasing trade turnover and joint projects.

item.title: Central Asian Foreign Ministers Meet to Discuss Cooperation and Future Summit
item.description: Foreign ministers from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) convened in Turkmenistan's "Awaza" national tourist zone to assess current cooperation and outline future development paths. The meeting, described as trusting and productive, emphasized strengthening multilateral ties and aligning perspectives on various issues. Discussions also focused on preparations for the upcoming CIS Heads of State Council meeting.

item.title: International Conference on Demographic Processes and Sustainable Development Held in Turkmenistan
item.description: An international conference titled "Demographic Processes and Sustainable Development: Modern Challenges and International Experience" took place in Turkmenistan's "Awaza" national tourist zone. The event gathered participants from Turkmenistan's parliament, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, CIS countries, and UN specialized agencies. Discussions focused on the role of demographic processes in sustainable socio-economic development and aligning global approaches to demographic situations.

item.title: Australian Lindian to Invest $150 Million in Former Kazatomprom Plant
item.description: Australian company Lindian Resources will invest $150 million in a former Kazatomprom plant in Stepnogorsk through its subsidiary Silkway Metals. The investment will modernize the facility and build a new workshop to produce rare earth metal carbonate. The project is slated for 2026-2028.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev arrives in Turkmenistan for working visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Turkmenistan for a working visit. He was met at the airport by Turkmenistan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Foreign Minister, Rashid Meredov. Tokayev is scheduled to attend the 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan, a CIS Heads of State Council meeting, and the Caspian Ecological Summit.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Visits Turkmenistan for Working Visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Turkmenistan for a working visit on October 8-9. He was met by Turkmenistan's Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov. Tokayev will attend the 8th Consultative Meeting of Central Asian and Azerbaijani Heads of State, a CIS Heads of State Council meeting, and the Caspian Ecological Summit in Avaza.

item.title: 45 MW Power Plant Under Construction in Taraz Industrial Zone
item.description: A 45 MW power plant is being built in the Taraz industrial zone to supply energy to the zone's infrastructure. The project's total investment is 235.6 billion tenge, intended for 12 other projects. Construction is 60% complete, with all necessary equipment delivered. The plant is scheduled for commissioning by December 15, 2026.

item.title: KazAvtoZhol Explains Cost Adjustments for Two Road Projects Totaling Nearly 10 Billion Tenge
item.description: KazAvtoZhol has clarified why costs were adjusted for two road projects totaling approximately 9.8 billion tenge. One project involves the medium repair of an 87 km section of the M-32 highway, contracted for 9.803 billion tenge. A second, larger project, 'Ulgaysyn–Sekseuil,' aims to upgrade a road to Category Ib by 2030.

item.title: Taliban Forcibly Evict Kabul Residents, Impose Rent on Self-Built Homes
item.description: Local sources report the Taliban are forcibly evicting residents from Omid-e Sabz Township in western Kabul, refusing to hear grievances. At least 30 homes have been vacated and occupied by Taliban families. Property owners who refused to pay imposed rent were forced out. The township has been declared "state-owned" by the Taliban Ministry of Justice.

item.title: Taliban Order Omid-e Sabz Residents to Pay 4,000 Afghanis Per Room Rent
item.description: Sources report the Taliban have ordered residents of Omid-e Sabz Township to pay 4,000 Afghanis per room rent, effective from the start of the current solar year. They must also pay six months' rent in advance. The Taliban have set the rent for their own members at 1,000 Afghanis per room. The Ministry of Justice has declared the township "state property" and ordered evacuations.

item.title: Taliban Ban Photos and Videos on Government Computers in Kandahar
item.description: The Taliban in Kandahar have ordered government departments to ban the use of photos and videos on computers and mobile phones. The directive, issued under the Law for the Propagation of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, requires strict implementation during official events.

item.title: Kazakh Consulate Meets Detained Citizens in Istanbul Amid Asylum Request Issues
item.description: Kazakhstan's consulate in Istanbul met with two detained citizens. The individuals were transferred to a deportation center where their return to Kazakhstan will be decided. One detainee's mother reported her son was forcibly sent to Istanbul after his asylum request in Moldova was rejected. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is monitoring the situation.

item.title: Kandahar Hospital Faces Severe Shortages of Medicine and Equipment, Patients Report
item.description: Patients at Mirwais Regional Hospital in Kandahar report critical shortages of medicine and equipment, forcing them to purchase supplies themselves. Health sources confirm financial problems hinder the hospital's ability to provide timely services. The 400-bed facility faces shortages in medical equipment and personnel, impacting patient care.

item.title: Putin's 2001 Bundestag Speech: Russia's Stance on Terrorism and Central Asia
item.description: In a historic 2001 speech to the German Bundestag, Russian President Vladimir Putin declared support for the US post-9/11, offering intelligence sharing and overflight rights. He also pledged support for the Northern Alliance against the Taliban and stated Russia would not oppose US military bases in Central Asia.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expanding Investment Opportunities Beyond Raw Materials, Report States
item.description: A World Financial Review analysis highlights Kazakhstan's economic diversification and investment potential. Despite significant foreign investment and industrial growth, the economy historically relied on natural resources. President Tokayev prioritizes diversifying into manufacturing and modernizing infrastructure to reduce raw material dependency.

item.title: Kazakhstan Modifies Procedures for Tax Deferral and Installment Payments
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated its regulations for deferring and making installment payments for taxes. Applicants will now be granted time to correct errors in submitted documents, with the original submission date preserved. This change aims to streamline the process, ensuring applications are processed within the standard timeframe if corrections are made promptly.

item.title: Almaty Residents Can Report Heating Issues After October 10 to New Hotline
item.description: Almaty has established an operational response headquarters to handle heating outages, leaks, or malfunctions after October 10. Residents can report issues via hotline 109, a unified dispatch center, management companies, social media, or the e-Otinish platform.

item.title: Former priest sentenced to four years in prison in Almaty for drug possession
item.description: A former Russian Orthodox priest, Iakov Vorontsov, has been sentenced to four years in prison in Almaty. He was found guilty of illegal possession of 2.44 grams of a synthetic drug, an amount considered very large. His sentence was reduced due to an amnesty related to Kazakhstan's new constitution.

item.title: 90% of Cybercrimes in Uzbekistan Originate from Abroad, Affecting One in Two Crimes
item.description: Approximately 90% of cybercrimes committed in Uzbekistan are perpetrated from foreign countries. Currently, nearly half of all crimes in the country are carried out using information technology. This trend highlights a significant cross-border challenge in combating digital offenses.

item.title: Two Streets in Astana to Be Partially Closed for LRT Construction
item.description: Partial traffic restrictions will be implemented on Syganak Street and Aytmatov Street in Astana starting October 7 due to the construction of the second phase of the Tarlan Astana light rail transit (LRT) project. Drivers are advised to plan routes accordingly.

item.title: Truck Queues Form at Kazakhstan-Russia Border Due to Checkpoint Reconstruction
item.description: Queues of trucks have formed at the Kazakhstan-Russia border due to reconstruction at the 'Kairak' checkpoint in the Kostanay region. State Revenue Department reports that narrowed lanes temporarily reduced throughput, exacerbated by seasonal agricultural and transit cargo increases.

item.title: Putin to Meet Iranian President in Turkmenistan during CIS Summit
item.description: Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov announced that Vladimir Putin will meet his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the CIS summit in Turkmenistan on October 8-9. Nine CIS heads of state confirmed their participation, with Iran invited for the first time.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Discuss Transport and Green Energy Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium discussed developing the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route and attracting Belgian technology for infrastructure modernization. They also explored industrial cooperation, critical raw material processing, and green technologies. Both sides expressed interest in joint projects.

item.title: Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases by 5.6 Tenge in One Day
item.description: The average weighted dollar exchange rate on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE) fell by 5.6 tenge, reaching 447.14 tenge. The official rate set by the National Bank of Kazakhstan for October 7 was 453.65 tenge. Exchange rates in Astana and Almaty also saw fluctuations.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran Fully Implement Visa-Free Travel Regime
item.description: Tajikistan and Iran have fully implemented a visa-free regime, allowing citizens of both countries to travel without a visa for up to 30 days within a 90-day period. This measure applies to ordinary foreign passports and is facilitated through international border crossings.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Reviews Proposals for New Ministry of Education and Science
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals for organizing the activities of the new Ministry of Education and Science. The ministry is tasked with ensuring continuity from preschool to higher education and managing the system with a unified approach.

item.title: Russia ready to help resolve Taliban-Pakistan disputes, says envoy
item.description: Russia is prepared to cooperate with regional partners to mediate disputes between the Taliban and Pakistan, according to Russian special envoy Zamir Kabulov. He stated that Western countries will not be involved in these resolution efforts. Moscow is interested in regional stability and believes it can play a mediating role.

item.title: 90% of Cybercrimes in Uzbekistan Committed from Abroad, Reports Interior Ministry
item.description: Nearly half of all crimes in Uzbekistan involve information technology, with 90% of cybercrimes being transnational and originating from abroad, according to Deputy Interior Minister Ramazon Ashrapov. He urged the public to be vigilant against fraud, emphasizing that combating these crimes requires public cooperation. Ashrapov outlined key cybersecurity rules for citizens to follow.

item.title: Lithuania Reconsiders Labor Migration Policy, Restricting Central Asian Workers Amidst Security Concerns
item.description: Lithuania is reviewing its labor migration policy towards Central Asia, halting applications from Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan and closing visa centers in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan from November 1. Officials cite administrative overload and security risks, occurring against a backdrop of incidents targeting the Muslim community. This shift impacts Central Asian migrants seeking alternatives to Russia.

item.title: World Bank Raises Uzbekistan's Economic Growth Forecast to 7.9% for 2026
item.description: The World Bank has increased its forecast for Uzbekistan's GDP growth to 7.9% for 2026, up from 6.4% in April. The revised figures, part of a report on Europe and Central Asia's economy, also project growth to 7.5% in 2027 and 7.1% in 2028. This growth is attributed to increased domestic demand, remittances, and structural reforms.
